blueprint_concepts: Basic elements of the standard hyperbola: focus, directrix, axis, latus rectum
Basic elements of the standard ellipse: focus, directrix, axis, latus rectum
english: Let $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ $(a>b>0)$ be an ellipse with eccentricity $e_{1}$, and let $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{A^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{B^{2}}=1$ $(A>0,B>0)$ be a hyperbola with eccentricity $e_{2}$, such that each latus rectum of $E$ is also a latus rectum of $H$. If $e_{2}=\dfrac{5}{4}$, then the value of $e_{1}-e_{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ $(a>b>0)$ उत्केन्द्रता $e_{1}$ वाला एक दीर्घवृत्त है, तथा $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{A^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{B^{2}}=1$ $(A>0,B>0)$ उत्केन्द्रता $e_{2}$ वाला एक अतिपरवलय है, जहाँ $E$ का प्रत्येक नाभिलम्ब $H$ का भी एक नाभिलम्ब है। यदि $e_{2}=\dfrac{5}{4}$ है, तो $e_{1}-e_{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Common latera recta $\Rightarrow$ same foci $(\pm c,0)$ and equal semi-latera recta: $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{B^{2}}{A}$
solution_full: The latera recta of $E$ are the chords $x=\pm c$ through its foci $(\pm c,0)$, $c=ae_{1}$, of half-length $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a}$. The latera recta of $H$ are the chords $x=\pm C$ through its foci $(\pm C,0)$, $C=Ae_{2}$, of half-length $\dfrac{B^{2}}{A}$.
If each latus rectum of $E$ is a latus rectum of $H$, the lines coincide, so $C=c$ (the foci are common), and the end points coincide, so $\dfrac{b^{2}}{a}=\dfrac{B^{2}}{A}$.
Equating and cancelling $c$: $\dfrac{1}{e_{1}}-e_{1}=e_{2}-\dfrac{1}{e_{2}}$. With $e_{2}=\dfrac{5}{4}$ the right side is $\dfrac{5}{4}-\dfrac{4}{5}=\dfrac{9}{20}$.

Remark: $\dfrac{1}{e_{1}}-e_{1}=e_{2}-\dfrac{1}{e_{2}}$ is satisfied by $e_{1}=\dfrac{1}{e_{2}}$, and the function $t\mapsto\dfrac{1}{t}-t$ is one-one on $(0,1)$, so always $e_{1}e_{2}=1$. For example $c=4$: $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}=1$ and $H:\dfrac{x^{2}}{(16/5)^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{144/25}=1$, both with semi-latus rectum $\dfrac{9}{5}$.
originality_note: New: an ellipse and a hyperbola sharing their latera recta; the shared latus rectum forces e1 e2 = 1 for every size (way 4, hidden invariant). Closest known: 2026-P2-Q13, where reciprocal eccentricities and common foci are given as data. Different because: here the reciprocity is not given but must be derived from the common latera recta, and no size data is supplied.

concept_use.Basic elements of the standard hyperbola: For H: foci (plus or minus A e2, 0), latus rectum half-length B^2/A = A(e2^2 - 1), written in terms of c and e2.
concept_use.Basic elements of the standard ellipse:: For E: foci (plus or minus a e1, 0), latus rectum half-length b^2/a = a(1 - e1^2), written in terms of c and e1; equating gives the equation for e1.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and symbol is introduced, every condition is stated, there is one reading of each sentence; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no asymptote wording. Checked that 'each latus rectum of E is also a latus rectum of H' forces common foci and equal half-lengths, that no size data is needed because c cancels, and that the answer -0.45 is exact. Changed: No change.
key_step: Common latera recta give c common and b^2/a = B^2/A, which reduces to 1/e1 - e1 = e2 - 1/e2.
justification: Two ideas linked (ellipse and hyperbola elements) with a hidden invariant: the data contain no size, so the student must see that c cancels. Close to 2026-P2-Q13 (L3), which uses reciprocal eccentricities with common foci.
